Quick note — our current agreement with Redwood is up Aug 15. We've had a tough budget quarter and the CFO is pushing to reduce SaaS spend across the board. Another vendor has proposed a lower price for similar inference throughput and is offering a 12-month promotional rate.

I've attached our Q2 usage report for reference (usage_report_Q2.csv).

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Stephanie — ran the numbers with finance. QuantaMed is mid-MRR but strategic (healthcare vertical, potential for expansion). Based on current usage and projected ramp, here are concession scenarios and P&L impact (annualized):

Option A (standard): 10% one-time renewal credit + 12-month term reset = ~3% ARR hit (acceptable)
Option B (escalated, retention package): 18-20% one-time credit + 12-month term reset + elevated SLA (99.9% uptime window with service credit up to 20% of monthly invoice for qualifying incidents) = ~9-11% ARR impact (requires exec sign-off)
Option C (deeper concession): 25% credit + 9-month term reset + expanded support SLAs = ~14% ARR impact (only for off-cycle approvals; not recommended)

Rationale for Option B: keeps revenue on the platform, prevents churn to a competitor, and preserves upsell motion for next 12 months. We can protect unit economics with tighter commit on usage threshold and minimum billing floors. Legal has sketched an SLA addendum — attaching draft (SLA_addendum_draft.docx).

Asking: need executive approval for Option B (target ask: 20% credit + 12-month reset + SLA addendum with capped credits). Please escalate to Marissa for sign-off with a brief note summarizing the business case.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: renewal_proposal_Quantamed_2028-07-10.pdf, SLA_addendum_draft.docx, usage_report_Q2.csv

Ask: approval to offer the Option B retention package (we can close this week if we get sign-off). If you prefer a concession cap, Karthik suggested 18% as a compromise. Recommend we also pre-authorize Legal to issue a limited SLA addendum to speed signature.

If helpful, I'm happy to hop on a 15-min call.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Thanks for the clear summary. I approve a retention package with these limits:

- One-time renewal credit: 18% (to be applied to the renewal invoice)
- Term reset: 12 months starting Aug 15
- SLA addendum: elevated uptime guarantee for production clinical endpoints; approve service credit language but cap aggregate credits at 15% of monthly invoice in any 12-month period.
- Pre-authorize Legal to prepare the addendum and Marketing to approve customer-facing language.

Conditions: require minimum committed usage floor to avoid abuse (we'll set a 3-month average baseline), and include a clause that credits are forfeited if QuantaMed reduces committed throughput below baseline levels. Karthik, work with Finance to confirm final ARR impact and ensure bookkeeping for the one-time credit. Stephanie, please send the revised proposal to Anna and Procurement with a 48-hour review window.

Once Anna signs, route to Legal for countersignature. Add the HubSpot deal link to the thread for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-2028-0421
